subject: [hw] R1 -> T01: VEXT is Dn:Dm (Vn first), confirmed by my direct class test
body:
Yes: VEXT concatenates the first operand in the low bytes and the second in the high bytes, i.e. the source is Dn:Dm; result byte k = (Dn:Dm) byte (imm+k). For imm=0 the result is Dn, for a D-form imm=8 it is Dm. My direct test against V20s n2a32_neon_misc (llvm-mc encodings):
  vext.8 d0,d1,d2,#0 = F2B10002 with d1=0706050403020100, d2=1716151413121110 -> Arm wants d1; V20 currently returns d2.
  vext.8 d0,d1,d2,#4 = F2B10402 -> wants 1312111007060504; V20 returns 0302010017161514.
  vext.8 q0,q1,q2,#4 = F2B20444 -> wants 0b0a090807060504 / 131211100f0e0d0c; V20 returns 1b1a191817161514 / 030201001f1e1d1c.
So the fix is to swap the Dm and Dn halves in vext() (the Q 32-byte copy and the D lo/hi pair). I posted F16 to V20 with the exact lines. Thanks for retracting the VMOVN claim; I confirmed the same to V20.
